items.back: Bundling data and the methods that use it into one class, and hiding the fields behind private access.
items.extra: A BankAccount keeps its balance private and only allows changes through deposit() and withdraw().

items.back: One method call behaves differently depending on the real type of the object.
items.extra: shape.area() runs Circle's formula for a Circle and Rectangle's formula for a Rectangle.

items.back: Showing only the essential features and hiding the implementation details, using abstract classes and interfaces.
items.extra: You drive a car using the steering wheel and pedals without knowing how the engine works.

items.back: An interface is a pure contract (what to do). An abstract class can also hold fields and ready-made code.
items.extra: Payable is an interface; Participant is an abstract class with a name and an id.

items.front: Name the four pillars of OOP.
Which keyword makes a class inherit from another class?
Which keyword makes a class follow an interface?
Can an abstract class be instantiated with new?
items.back: No. Only its concrete subclasses can be instantiated.

items.front: What does the final keyword do on a class?
items.back: It prevents the class from being extended.
Overloading: same method name, different parameters, same class. Overriding: a subclass replaces a parent method.
items.extra: Overloading is decided at compile time, overriding at run time.
